description.narrative: Overall objectiveTo deliver accountability for crimes committed under the previous regime and strengthen professional, civilian-led security institutions, ensuring continuity of internal and regional security as ECOMIG gradually withdraws. Specific objectivesOperationalise transitional justice commitments by supporting domestic investigations and prosecutions arising from TRRC recommendations, ensuring accountability and deterrence against future abuses.Improve justice and security system performance, moving from policy frameworks to measurable results through case-tracking and performance pilots.Strengthen capacity and professionalism across the security sector, including through unified training and doctrine as a means to reinforce discipline, cohesion and civilian oversight. Enable the Special Accountability Mechanism to conduct credible investigations and fair domestic trials, strengthening public trust in state institutions.Expected main outputsSystematised oversight mechanisms for White Paper implementation, including structured coordination led by the Office of National Security and regular monitoring inputs from the National Human Rights Commission, the Ombudsman and civil society.Operational case-tracking systems established for TRRC-related investigations and prosecutions, and for selected SSR performance pilots (e.g. SGBV).Security-sector planning and budgeting processes strengthened, including joint planning tools aligned with the National Security Act.A unified National Training Framework developed and applied, supporting capacity and professionalism across security institutions, including the Gambia Armed Forces, with links to regional centres of excellence through exchange programmes, regional Training-of-Trainers, and ECOWAS-aligned curricula.Enhanced investigative, prosecutorial and judicial capacities within the Special Prosecutor¿s Office and Special Criminal Division, including improved case preparation, fair-trial standards and victim-witness handling.
